biography: Born in the shadow of the Le Mans circuit, Claude Ballot-Léna practically breathed gasoline from the moment he could walk. His father, a mechanic for a local racing team, instilled in him a love for speed and precision. Claude's early years were spent karting, tearing up local tracks and quickly outgrowing the junior leagues. A pivotal moment came at age 16 when, during a practice session, he flawlessly executed a daring overtake around a notoriously difficult corner, earning the attention of a Porsche talent scout. This led to a spot in a regional Porsche-sponsored racing program, catapulting him into the world of GT racing. Now, at 23, Claude is making waves driving a Porsche 911 RSR 74, steadily climbing the ranks and proving his mettle in the fiercely competitive world of endurance racing. His consistency and level-headedness belie his age, making him a driver to watch in the coming years.
drivingStyle: Claude's driving style is best described as calculated aggression. He doesn't often make flashy, high-risk maneuvers, but instead focuses on maintaining consistent lap times and preserving his equipment. He's known for his exceptional tire management, often nursing his rubber further than his competitors. In corners, he favors a smooth, precise entry, carrying maximum speed through the apex and setting up for a clean exit. Under pressure, Claude remains remarkably calm, rarely making mistakes and capitalizing on the errors of others. This steady approach makes him a formidable endurance racer.

careerHighlight: Winning the Spa 24 Hours in his rookie year, showcasing exceptional endurance and strategic driving to secure a surprise victory for his team.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the Le Mans 24 Hours due to a mechanical failure while leading his class, a heartbreaking end to a promising race.
